    AI Overview
    Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) is a public research university in Richmond, Virginia, founded in 1838. Known for its extensive health sciences programs, top-tier research, and urban campus, it serves over 29,000 students. The VCU Rams basketball team is notable for regular NCAA tournament appearances, competing in the Atlantic 10 Conference. 
    Key Details About VCU: 
    • Location: Richmond, Virginia.
    • Established: 1838 (as Hampden-Sydney medical department), merged in 1968.
    • Enrollment: Over 29,000 students, including over 21,000 undergraduates.
    • Academics: Offers over 200 degree and certificate programs across 17 colleges and schools.
    • Rankings & Research: Top 50 in national research expenditures, according to the National Science Foundation, with over
      million in sponsored research in 2024.
    • Athletics: Competes as the Virginia Commonwealth University Rams in Division I (A-10 Conference), known for a 2011 Final Four run and frequent tournament appearances.
    • Health System: VCU Health includes schools of medicine, dentistry, nursing, and pharmacy. 
    Key Takeaways: 
    • Admission: Features a high (>90%) acceptance rate, with guaranteed admission for certain GPAs.
    • Urban Campus: Integrated into downtown Richmond, often described as a "hidden gem" urban research institution.
    • 2026 Season: The 2026 men's basketball team qualified for the NCAA tournament and achieved a first-round upset of North Carolina.

    AI Overview
    The VCU Rams represent
    Virginia Commonwealth University in Richmond, Virginia, competing in the Atlantic 10 Conference (A-10). In 2026, they are a 11th-seeded, 27-7 team known for strong 3-point shooting and high-pressure defense, facing North Carolina in the NCAA Tournament first round after winning the A-10 Tournament. 
    Key Details for 2026 Season 
    • Head Coach: Phil Martelli Jr. (first-year).
    • Record: 27-7 (won A-10 Championship).
    • Key Players: Leading scorer and guard Terrance Hill Jr., along with center Lazar Djokovic.
    • Style: Ranked 15th nationally in 3-point percentage (
      ).
    • Tournament Reputation: Known as a "bracket buster," VCU has 21 NCAA Tournament appearances (as of 2026) and a memorable 2011 Final Four run. 
    2026 NCAA Tournament
    As an 11-seed in the 2026 South Region, VCU is considered a dangerous opponent, having won 16 of their last 17 games leading into the matchup with 6th-seeded North Carolina.
